clue.text: Under the impression some emotion is called for

definitions.meaning: having a hunch or belief that something is so, as in 'I have a sense that'
a sentiment or mood experienced inwardly

explanation.surface: Someone senses that a display of emotion is required.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a hunch (being under an impression) and an emotion such as joy or anger.

clue.text: Slump. — the people in office needed to raise the standard

parts.note: to flag is to droop or tire
the staff are the workers in an office

explanation.surface: In a downturn, office workers must lift standards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standard' looks like a level of quality but is a flag, which a pole raises.
explanation.definitionFit: A pole hoists a flag, and a standard is a flag.

clue.text: Succeeded without right, that's for certain

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the letters for succeeded go round the other piece

parts.note: ensued means followed on, succeeded

explanation.surface: Someone won without being in the right, that much is sure.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made sure is guaranteed, so certain.

clue.text: Being disrespectful about the rebel leader is not wise!

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the cheeky word goes round the other letter

parts.note: impudent means cheeky, disrespectful

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Insulting the leader of a rebellion is a foolish move.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwise or rash conduct is lacking in good sense.

clue.text: Last appearance of the Cheshire Cat in Wagnerian opera's finale

definitions.text: Last appearance of the Cheshire Cat

indicators.note: only the closing part of the opera's title is kept, the opening letters dropped

parts.note: Lohengrin is an opera by Wagner

explanation.surface: The Cheshire Cat makes a final appearance at the end of a Wagner opera.
explanation.walkthrough: In Alice in Wonderland, the Cheshire Cat fades away until only its smile remains.
explanation.definitionFit: In Lewis Carroll's story the cat vanishes leaving only its smile, the last thing seen of it.

clue.text: A way a twitch is apt to move about

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a nervous twitch tends to make a person fidget.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics an astatic instrument has no fixed orientation, so it is unstable and liable to shift position.

clue.text: Arouse hostility against one possibility

indicators.note: a possibility is one possible arrangement, so the letters of the preceding words may be reordered

explanation.surface: One option may provoke opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: To make an enemy of someone is to provoke their hostility.

clue.text: The heartless "X" put up for conviction

indicators.note: the heart of the three-letter word is its middle letter, which is removed
in a down clue, put up means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A cross is marked on a ballot paper for a criminal sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns TEN into NET, after TE.
explanation.definitionFit: A principle firmly held is a belief or conviction.

clue.text: First trainee in the plant

indicators.note: in means placed inside the next word

parts.note: 1st is written as IST, with I for one
L is for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: The first apprentice is set to work in the factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a factory but is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: This prickly flowering weed is the emblem of Scotland.

clue.text: A bit of pontoon or some other game

definitions.meaning: one of the planks forming the deck of a pontoon bridge
a board game, different from pontoon the card game

explanation.surface: Someone plays a hand of the card game pontoon or tries a different game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pontoon' suggests the card game, which makes 'other game' feel natural, but the first sense is a floating bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a deck plank on a floating bridge and the board game with kings and queens.

clue.text: Moralist taking a retrogressive attitude

indicators.note: going backwards, so the word for attitude is read from end to start

parts.note: a pose is a bodily or mental attitude

explanation.surface: A preacher of morals holds old-fashioned, backward-looking views.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrogressive' turns POSE into ESOP, which follows A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek fabulist's tales each end with a moral, making him a classic moralist.

clue.text: Even in its crude form it's quite concentrated

indicators.note: a crude form is a rough, unrefined version, so the letters before it are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Something is potent even when it is unrefined.
explanation.definitionFit: Intensive effort or farming is concentrated in a small area or short time.

clue.text: Spring in Brussels

definitions.meaning: to spring up is to shoot or grow
the Brussels vegetable, a small green cabbage-like bud

explanation.surface: Springtime arrives in the Belgian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link. 'Brussels' looks like the city but stands for the vegetable named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoot up is to grow from seed, and the small green vegetable is called after the Belgian city.

clue.text: When stoned it causes alarm

indicators.note: 'When stoned' tells us that the little word it is to be set among stones, so it goes inside them

parts.note: agates are semi-precious stones, so stoned suggests agates
taken as written

explanation.surface: Being high on drugs leaves someone frightened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stoned' looks like drug slang, but here IT is surrounded by AGATES, the stones.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up and disturb someone is to make them anxious, which is causing alarm.

clue.text: Indulgence shown when a scholar turned up the 'answer

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a scholar
a solution is an answer

explanation.surface: A student shows up with the answer and is pardoned.
explanation.definitionFit: In church terms an indulgence and a priest's pardon both remit sins.

clue.text: Sum up the French muddle

parts.note: to sum up figures is to add them
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Doing arithmetic in French leaves someone confused.
explanation.definitionFit: To confuse or befuddle the mind is to muddle it.

clue.text: A person who finds work telling

definitions.text: A person who finds work telling

parts.words: A person who finds work telling
parts.note: a teller is the person at a bank counter who counts money, so 'telling' is the job, not something revealing

explanation.definitionFit: A cashier at a bank counter is called a teller, so telling is literally the work.

clue.text: Falls, as many a seafaring man does

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many
a tar is a sailor
acts means does

explanation.surface: Many a sailor tumbles over.
explanation.definitionFit: Large waterfalls are called by this name, as are steep river rapids.

clue.text: The builders of Kew longed for instruction

indicators.note: builders assemble material, so the letters of the next words are built into a new order

explanation.surface: Those who built Kew Gardens yearned for training.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning gained through teaching is what instruction gives.

clue.text: Bill being content, isn't for changing parts

indicators.note: being the contents means sitting inside the other letters
changing means the letters before it are moved around

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A bill is accepted, though it is not open to amendment in places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' scrambles ISNT FOR into FRTIONS; 'being content' puts AC inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fractions are portions of a whole, such as halves and quarters.

clue.text: It demands a lively performance

parts.note: a musical direction on a score asking players to perform with spirit

explanation.definitionFit: The Italian musical term tells performers to play in an animated way.

clue.text: A poet in debt — as so many are

indicators.note: the poet's name sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A poet is short of money, like so many of them.
explanation.walkthrough: The rest of the clue ('many are') adds to the joke about poets being broke.
explanation.definitionFit: Torquato Tasso was the Italian Renaissance poet who wrote Jerusalem Delivered.

clue.text: One enjoying a peaceful retirement

parts.note: 'retirement' suggests leaving work, but it means retiring to bed for the night

explanation.definitionFit: Someone retired to bed and resting soundly is slumbering.

clue.text: Locks present no problem for him!

definitions.text: Locks present no problem for him!

parts.words: Locks present no problem for him!
parts.note: 'Locks' suggests door locks for a burglar, but it means locks of hair, which a hairdresser deals with easily

explanation.definitionFit: A hairdresser handles locks of hair every day.

clue.text: Tea — exceptionally large order has disappeared

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
OS stands for outsize, exceptionally large

explanation.surface: A huge tea order has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' looks like a request for goods but is orderliness.
explanation.definitionFit: Complete disorder is the state where all organisation is gone.

clue.text: An abundance of things to eat left inside

indicators.note: inside means placed within the other piece

parts.note: food is things to eat

explanation.surface: Plenty of food remains in the larder.
explanation.definitionFit: A torrent or overflow of anything is a great quantity of it.

clue.text: Test an alternative to wood

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
deal is pine or fir timber

explanation.surface: Someone is trialling a substitute for timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial by ordeal was a test of guilt, and any severe trial is one.

clue.text: Make a move to provide porridge

definitions.meaning: British slang for a prison sentence

explanation.surface: Someone gets moving to cook breakfast oats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'porridge' is British slang for time served in prison, and so is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To budge is to shift, and both words are British slang for jail time.

clue.text: Articles to fog a man of science

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a is the other form of the indefinite article
taken as written
mist is a light fog

explanation.surface: Papers are written to confuse a scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissecting expert who studies body structure is a scientist.

clue.text: Carried on wearing a vestment

definitions.meaning: managed or got by in difficulty
dressed in a cope, a long cloak worn by priests

explanation.surface: A priest went on with the service in robes.
explanation.definitionFit: To manage is to get by, and a cope is a priest's cloak, so one wearing it is clad that way.

clue.text: Breaking down on downs or mountain

indicators.note: breaking down means taking apart, so the letters of the next words are reassembled

explanation.surface: A walker is collapsing on the hills or the peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking down' rearranges ON DOWNS. The answer is the highest mountain in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the highest peak in Wales.

clue.text: Book an extra player

definitions.meaning: to book is to set aside in advance
a substitute kept on the bench

explanation.surface: A team books an additional player.
explanation.definitionFit: To book a table is to keep it aside, and a substitute in a squad is a spare player.
